caption: The drawing consists of a technical, architectural-style blueprint rendered in black and red lines on a beige or off-white background. The main objects appear to be three orthographic views—front, side, and top—of a standing piece of furniture with an oval shape at the top, likely a mirror, suspended between two vertical posts with finials. Below the mirror, there is a structure with curved supports leading to a central stem that connects to a curved base with three outward-extending feet, typical of a tripod stand. There are additional curved and straight cross-sections shown, including a small, downward-facing concave curve (possibly a drawer or basin) under the center. The composition is overlaid with meticulously labeled red measurement lines both horizontally and vertically, specifying various dimensions such as heights, widths, and radii. Notable measurements include overall heights, segment lengths, and radii of curves, as well as the scale annotation “1 1/2 IN. TO 1 FT.” written at the bottom left of the drawing.
title: Pole Screen and Candlestand
